method.purpose: Compare actual WLD, EWI and exporter integration operations before and after sharing SDK algorithms.
method: Five independent processes per implementation and fixture profile, three implementations.
Alternate original/previous/optimized and optimized/previous/original order; timed processes run serially.
GOMAXPROCS=2 and GOGC=100 in both modes.
Fixed operation counts, same fixtures and output correctness checks.
Do not drop slow samples. Report medians and ranges.
CPU and peak RSS measured for the whole precompiled child; compilation excluded.
Heap/GC instrumentation is a separate run from Go benchmark latency.
Retained heap after forced GC is not allocation traffic or peak RSS.
Runtime tests use fixture clients; they do not prove production apiserver or live-controller capacity.
Describe changes above 5% as potentially material; do not infer equivalence from overlapping/noisy ranges.
method.goal: Reduce measured integration overhead while preserving public APIs, validation, complete outputs and fixture/cache policies.
acceptance: Preserve all original benchmark artifacts and fixed operation counts.
Correctness and race tests precede final timing.
No concurrent builds/tests while timing final samples.
Compare the unchanged historical algorithms and candidate in fresh alternating processes; publish regressions and all samples.
Five samples per mode/profile for final results; exploratory probes are labelled and kept separately.
No claim of universal perfection or production 100k capacity from bounded fixtures.

implementations.before: Original consumer algorithms, preserved frozen binary
implementations.previous: First SDK integration at c6cad432ab56, preserved frozen binary
implementations.after: Optimized adapter/SDK files recorded by source SHA256

method.comparison: Re-run all three implementations on the same workstation; preserve all previous measurements unchanged.

ewi-source-provenance.optimization: Complete typed definition conversion after DeepCopy replaces per-Parse JSON marshal/unmarshal; no cache, no retained state, no SDK changes required.
